interest: This document provides a concise administrative overview of the intersection between Japanese domestic industrial policy, imperial expansion, and international trade friction during the 1930s. It demonstrates how the Japanese state utilized subsidies, cartels, and regulatory legislation to foster strategic domestic industries—such as motor vehicles in Japan and Manchukuo—and subsequently established state-sponsored monopolies in occupied China, directly challenging foreign commercial rights. For historians, the file is particularly valuable as a concordance illustrating diplomatic friction over the Open Door policy and Western concessions (such as the Belgian tramway franchise in Tientsin), while providing direct cross-reference citations to the underlying State Department files.
overview: This file (894.602/565) consists of a single Department of State 'List of Papers' (Form DS-46), dated October 12, 1945, indexing seven cross-referenced documents generated between March 1934 and January 1939 under the subject of Japanese monopolies, concessions, franchises, contracts, bounties, and subsidies. The docket entries record diplomatic instructions and reporting concerning Japanese export trade subsidies, proposed legislation to control the automobile industry in Japan and Manchukuo, U.S. representations on the Open Door doctrine in China, the establishment of the Japanese-controlled Central China Silk Yarn Company monopoly, and Japanese infringements on the Belgian Tramway and Electric Company's concession in Tientsin. Because all underlying despatches and telegrams—originating primarily from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew, Chargé d'Affaires Edwin L. Neville, and the Department of State—were filed under other specific decimal classifications (including 611.9417, 894.797, 693.002, 893.6552, and 893.78), this sheet serves as the master index tracking Japanese industrial policy and economic expansionism in the 1930s.

subfiles.about: A Department of State docket sheet indexing cross-referenced diplomatic correspondence from 1934 to 1939 regarding Japanese monopolies, export subsidies, and industrial control.
subfiles.summary: This Department of State List of Papers (Form DS-46), dated October 12, 1945, indexes seven documents classified under or cross-referenced to decimal file 894.602 concerning Japanese monopolies, concessions, and subsidies between 1934 and 1939. The entries summarize reporting on Japanese export subsidies, automotive industry control legislation in Japan and Manchukuo, representations regarding the Open Door in China, the Central China Silk Yarn Company monopoly, and protests over infringements on the Belgian Tramway and Electric Company in Tientsin. Because each of the underlying communications was transferred to other decimal files, this docket list constitutes the entirety of the physical file.
